items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: I took J.J. Johnson’s place in Benny Carter’s orchestra, see?

ctx.x: So you were in the right place at the right time.

Right place at the right time, and I took J.J. Johnson’s place in Benny Carter’s orchestra, see? And I went out with Benny Carter and this was 1945, see? And then after that, Benny Carter had such a great band where Benny Carter was a person that was tremendous help in teaching more how to read, and play ad lib solos see? Because back in those days most of our jazz musicians were great jazz artists, but many of them could not read.
So they had to do much of it by ear?
